#!/bin/sh
# This is a runbook, not a script: open it, and paste ONE BLOCK AT A TIME into a console of the machine, as root.
case $- in *i*) ;; *) echo "This file is a runbook, not a script. Open it and paste one block at a time into a root console, reading what each one prints."; exit 1;; esac
#
# Upgrade of the operating system by hand: Debian 11 (bullseye) to Debian 12 (bookworm).
# Plan: p1-3f419de2f78c0f350957a354740452ff   made at 2026-10-12 09:30:16 UTC   (hop debian-11-12; it was good for 24 hours, until 2026-10-13 09:30 UTC)
#
# This text was written for exactly this machine and this plan. If the machine changed since (packages, sources, holds), ask for a new plan.
# Block 0 checks that the plan is not older than its 24 hours and that the sources of apt are the ones the plan was made from. The plan holds no identity of the machine, so
# nothing here knows WHICH machine this is: the name that you type guards the terminal (it shows that you looked at which machine you are on), not the identity of the machine.
# Do not adapt the text by hand.
# A NEW PLAN is made in the dashboard: open the Operating system window and press 'Make the plan again' (or 'See what the upgrade would do', the first time). A plan is good for 24 hours,
# and a text is written from one plan only. TO ASK FOR HELP is to ask whoever looks after this machine and its ReCasaOS (the person or the company that installed it for you), and to give them
# the text of the block, everything it printed, and the files that its STOP line names.
#
# THIS TEXT DOES NOT RUN THE READINESS REPORT. Read the report in the dashboard first, and do not start when it says that it refuses: it looks at what this text does not
# (the boot loader, the file systems, the packages that are built from source, and more). Block 0 looks at a few of those again (room in /boot, the EFI partition, the disk of grub-pc).
#
# WHAT YOU NEED BEFORE YOU START
#  - A snapshot of the machine (from the hypervisor), or a console that works without the network: a screen and a keyboard, a serial line, the
#    hypervisor's console. A tunnel (Tailscale, Cloudflare) does not count: it goes down with the network card.
#  - A terminal that survives a dropped connection, for blocks 5 and 6: the machine's own console, or tmux or screen. INSTALL tmux NOW, BEFORE block 3, while the machine is
#    still Debian 11 (apt-get install tmux): block 0 stops when there is no console and neither is installed. After block 3 install nothing by hand: a package installed from Debian 12's
#    sources upgrades libc6 with it, outside the protection of block 5. Become root first (su - or sudo -i), THEN start it from the root shell:  tmux new-session -s casaos-upgrade
#    (or: screen -S casaos-upgrade)  and paste the blocks inside it (sudo and su drop the variables that tmux and screen set: that is why). Blocks 5 and 6 stop if they are not run in one of
#    them or on a console. After a dropped connection: log in, become root, tmux attach -t casaos-upgrade   (or: screen -r casaos-upgrade). In block 5, libc6 restarts services (ssh, smbd and
#    cron were restarted in the measured hop): do not count on your connection staying up.
#  - A plain sh to paste into: if your root shell has aliases for mv, cp or rm, type sh first. The blocks use mv -f and read back what they wrote, but a plain sh is what they were tried in.
#    Type sh first too when a paste is changed on its way: bash without bracketed paste takes a TAB for completion, and a tab in a comment line of the sources of this machine then changes what block 3 writes
#    (block 3 sees it, stops on the hash, and stops again at every paste).
#  - Debian 11 fully updated and restarted once before you start (apt-get update, apt-get upgrade, restart), as the machine of the measurement was. Nothing here checks it.
#  - The machine must not be doing something else with its packages (no update running, no other package manager). Blocks 0, 3, 5 and 6 look at the processes of the package managers; the apt-get
#    commands of the blocks that check, download or install wait up to 5 minutes for the dpkg lock, and apt-get update does not wait for the lock of the lists: it fails at once when another one holds it.
#  - Room in /var/backups for a copy of /etc and /etc/apt. The directory that this text makes there is private to root (mode 700), because it holds a copy of /etc.
#  - Time: the measured hop took about two and a half minutes of apt on a fast network; the downloads and the configuration of a real machine take longer.
#
# WHAT THE PLAN SAYS
#  - apt would upgrade 384 packages, install 75 new ones and remove 2 (fuse, libsemanage1).
#  - You installed yourself: fuse. Block 3 asks you to type their names: that is accepting that they are removed.
#  - It downloads about 140 MB and takes about 300 MB more room on the disk (apt's own figures, rounded).
#  - Sources that are not Debian's are put aside for the hop: docker.list, line 5 of sources.list.
#  - 1 line(s) of backports are dropped.
#
# WHAT HAS BEEN TESTED, AND WHAT HAS NOT
#  - The apt COMMANDS of blocks 3 to 6 below, and their order (update, the download and the minimal upgrade, the download and the full upgrade, the simulation that finds nothing left), are
#    the ones of a hop from Debian 11 to Debian 12 that was measured in a virtual machine, on a clean cloud image with ReCasaOS and Docker installed, and that ended with the machine up on Debian 12,
#    but for one option: the measured hop ran them with Dpkg::Use-Pty=0, and this text leaves apt's pty on, so that /var/log/apt/term.log holds what dpkg and the scripts of the packages print.
#  - APT'S OWN PTY, WHICH THIS TEXT LEAVES ON, WAS NOT RUN IN THE MEASURED HOP. It was tried in a copy of a Debian 11 system, under script, never in that virtual machine and never in a real tmux, screen or console.
#    With it apt takes the terminal over while dpkg runs (raw mode: what you type goes on to dpkg, and what was pasted before is dropped): type nothing and paste nothing until the block has ended.
#  - THE REPAIR LADDER AND THE CATCH-UP PASSES OF BLOCK 6 WERE NOT RUN IN THAT HOP: it did not need them. They come from the release notes of Debian 12 (dpkg --configure -a, apt-get -f install,
#    the full upgrade again), and so do the simulations that block 6 makes before them. Never run for real, they may be wrong in ways nobody has seen.
#  - THIS TEXT AS A WHOLE HAS NOT BEEN RUN, END TO END, ON A MACHINE THAT BOOTED. The rest of it was not measured: the checks, the STOP lines, the snapshot, the comparison with the plan,
#    the restore script, the checks before the restart and the ones after it. They were tried against stand-in commands, never on a machine that was upgraded with this text:
#    timers, libc6 restarting services, the initrd, grub, the restart and Docker's source were never run for real. They may be wrong in ways nobody has seen.
#  - Your machine is not that image. It has its own hardware (network card names, firmware, disk controllers), its own history, files you edited, and packages that nobody tested.
#    None of that was tried, and nothing here promises how it will go.
#  - Nothing goes back to Debian 11 once the upgrade has begun (block 5): a failure after it is mended by going forward, or by the snapshot.
#  - A line that starts with STOP says why a block did not go through. But a command that fails in the middle (a full disk, a lost connection) ends a block too, with its own message and
#    no STOP line: a block that did not print 'Block N done.' did not go through, STOP line or not. Read what it printed, do not go on, and look at the table at the end.

# ==============================
# BLOCK 0 (of the blocks 0 to 8): check that this is the machine of the plan, and that it is ready
# Nothing is changed here. Type the name of this machine between the quotes of TYPED_HOSTNAME, so that you have looked at which machine this is (the plan holds no identity of the machine: this guards the terminal, nothing more).
# It also checks that the plan is still good (24 hours), that the sources of apt are the ones the plan was made from, that dpkg is quiet, that there is room (for the packages, in /usr and /, in /boot, on the EFI partition
# or the disk of grub-pc where the machine has them), that the tools the next blocks use are there (ps, ss, and curl when Docker's source is put aside), and that blocks 5 and 6 will have a terminal that survives a
# dropped connection: a console, or tmux or screen installed. If none is, this is the time to install one (apt-get install tmux): after block 3 the machine takes its packages from Debian 12.
# It does NOT run the readiness report of the dashboard: read that first, and do not start when it says that it refuses. It prints a WARNING, which is not a stop, when dkms has modules built from source.
# It looks at the processes of the package managers; it does not see their file locks. The apt-get commands of the blocks that check, download or install wait up to 5 minutes for the dpkg lock and stop if it stays
# held; apt-get update waits for no lock, and fails at once when another package manager holds the lock of the lists.
# Run it before block 3: once block 3 has begun, the sources of apt may no longer be the plan's, and this block says so. It also looks at the folders that another plan of this machine left in
# /var/backups: when that plan's block 3 ran, the sources are its own, and this block names the restore script of that plan (or, once its upgrade has begun, the words that only go forward).
# ==============================
# >>> BLOCK 0 verify
(
set -eu
LC_ALL=C; export LC_ALL
PATH=/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin; export PATH
BK=/var/backups/casaos-os-upgrade-p1-3f419de2f78c0f350957a354740452ff
[ ! -e "$BK/done-after" ] || { echo "STOP: the hop is over (block 8 ended: done-after is in $BK): there is nothing more to run in this text."; exit 1; }
for fin in /var/backups/casaos-os-upgrade-*; do
  [ ! -e "$fin/done-after" ] || { echo "STOP: the hop is over for this machine: the plan whose folder is $fin took it to the end (block 8 ended: done-after is there), and there is nothing more to run in this text."; exit 1; }
done
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive APT_LISTCHANGES_FRONTEND=none NEEDRESTART_SUSPEND=1
aptq() { apt-get -y -q -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=300 -o Acquire::Retries=3 -o Dpkg::Options::=--force-confdef -o Dpkg::Options::=--force-confold "$@"; }
# Type the name of this machine between the quotes, then run the block.
TYPED_HOSTNAME=""
echo "Block 0: is this the machine of the plan? Nothing is changed."
[ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] || { echo "STOP: run this as root."; exit 1; }
if [ -e "$BK/begun-upgrade" ] || [ -e "$BK/done-minimal" ]; then
  echo "STOP: the upgrade has begun (block 5 was started): this block is for before it. Do not restore anything. Only forward: finish with dpkg --configure -a, then apt-get -f install, then block 6 and the blocks after it (the table at the end of the runbook has the exact commands)."
  exit 1
fi
if [ -e "$BK/apt-orig" ]; then
  if [ -e "$BK/done-sources" ]; then
    echo "STOP: block 3 has begun and ended ($BK/done-sources is there): the sources of apt are Debian 12's now, and this block is for before it. The next is block 4. To start again from block 3, put the sources back first: sh $BK/restore-sources.sh   (it forgets blocks 3 and 4)."
  else
    echo "STOP: block 3 has begun and did not end ($BK/apt-orig is there): the sources of apt may no longer be the ones that the plan was made from, and this block is for before it. Look at the table at the end of this text: sh $BK/restore-sources.sh puts the sources back (when that file is there), and block 3 can then be run again."
  fi
  exit 1
fi
for d in /var/backups/casaos-os-upgrade-*; do
  if [ -e "$d/begun-upgrade" ] || [ -e "$d/done-minimal" ]; then
    echo "STOP: another plan of this machine has begun the upgrade of the packages ($d has begun-upgrade): Debian 11 and 12 are mixed there, and nothing in this text applies to it. Do not restore anything, and do not make another plan: finish that upgrade. Only forward: DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive dpkg --configure -a --force-confdef --force-confold   then:   DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -s -f install   (read it first: a line that starts with Remv is a package that it would remove; if it is one that the plan does not name, or one that this text protects, do not go on and ask for help)   then:   DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -y -o Dpkg::Options::=--force-confdef -o Dpkg::Options::=--force-confold -f install   then:   apt-get dist-upgrade until nothing is left, and restart. Or ask for help."
    exit 1
  fi
  if [ -e "$d/apt-orig" ]; then
    if [ -f "$d/restore-sources.sh" ]; then
      echo "STOP: block 3 of another plan of this machine began ($d/apt-orig is there), so the sources of apt may no longer be the ones that this plan was made from. Put them back first: sh $d/restore-sources.sh   (it puts the sources back as they were and takes apt-orig aside), then run this block again."
    else
      echo "STOP: block 3 of another plan of this machine began ($d/apt-orig is there), and $d/restore-sources.sh is not. apt-orig is the whole copy of /etc/apt that it made before it changed anything: compare it with /etc/apt, put back by hand what differs, rename apt-orig, then run this block again."
    fi
    exit 1
  fi
done
[ -n "$TYPED_HOSTNAME" ] && [ "$TYPED_HOSTNAME" = "$(hostname)" ] || { echo "STOP: this machine is called $(hostname). Type that name between the quotes of TYPED_HOSTNAME at the top of this block, to show that you are on the machine you mean to upgrade."; exit 1; }
[ "$(date +%s)" -lt 1791883816 ] || { echo "STOP: this plan is older than its 24 hours (it was good until 2026-10-13 09:30 UTC): the machine may have changed. Ask for a new plan."; exit 1; }
grep -q '^VERSION_CODENAME=bullseye$' /etc/os-release || { echo "STOP: this machine is not Debian 11 (bullseye) any more: the plan does not apply. Ask for a new one."; exit 1; }
audit="$(dpkg --audit 2>&1)" && [ -z "$audit" ] || { echo "STOP: dpkg is not quiet: it has a package that is half installed or half configured, or it cannot open its own database. dpkg --audit says: ${audit:-nothing, but it ended with an error}. Run: dpkg --configure -a   then ask for a new plan. If dpkg cannot open its own database, ask for help."; exit 1; }
command -v ss > /dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "STOP: ss is not installed: blocks 2 and 8 use it to write down the ports that listen. Install it: apt-get install iproute2   then run this block again."; exit 1; }
command -v curl > /dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "STOP: curl is not installed: block 8 uses it to ask whether Docker publishes its repository for bookworm. Install it: apt-get install curl   then run this block again."; exit 1; }
if [ -z "${TMUX:-}${STY:-}" ]; then
  case "$(tty 2> /dev/null || true)" in
    /dev/tty[0-9]*|/dev/hvc*|/dev/ttyS*) ;;
    *) command -v tmux > /dev/null 2>&1 || command -v screen > /dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "STOP: there is no console here, and neither tmux nor screen is installed: blocks 5 and 6 need one, and after block 3 it is too late to install it (a package installed from Debian 12's sources upgrades libc6 with it, outside block 5's protection). Install it now, while this is still Debian 11:  apt-get install tmux   then run this block again."; exit 1; } ;;
  esac
fi
psout="$(ps -eo comm=,args= 2> /dev/null)" || { echo "STOP: ps did not answer, so the processes cannot be looked at for a package manager. If ps is not installed: apt-get install procps   then run this block again."; exit 1; }
busy="$(printf '%s\n' "$psout" | awk '
$1 == "apt" || $1 == "apt-get" || $1 == "aptitude" || $1 == "apt.systemd.dai" { $1 = $1; print substr($0, 1, 120); exit }
$1 == "dpkg" { for (i = 2; i <= NF; i++) if ($i ~ /^(-i|-r|-P|--install|--configure|--unpack|--remove|--purge|--triggers-only)$/) { $1 = $1; print substr($0, 1, 120); exit } }
$2 ~ /\/unattended-upgrade$/ || ($2 ~ /(^|\/)python[0-9.]*$/ && $3 ~ /\/unattended-upgrade$/) { $1 = $1; print substr($0, 1, 120); exit }
' | tr -cd '\040-\176')"
[ -z "$busy" ] || { echo "STOP: a package manager is running (the process list says: $busy): wait until it ends. This check looks at the processes, not at the file locks of apt and dpkg: the apt-get commands of this text that check, download or install wait up to 5 minutes for the dpkg lock and stop if it stays held, and apt-get update does not wait for the lock of the lists."; exit 1; }
aptq check > /dev/null || { echo "STOP: apt-get check finds a broken dependency, or could not get the lock of dpkg in 5 minutes (what it printed above says which): repair it, or wait for the other package manager, then run this block again. If it is a broken dependency, ask for a new plan once it is repaired."; exit 1; }
avail() { df -Pk "$1" | awk 'NR == 2 { print $4 }'; }
[ "$(avail '/var/cache/apt/archives')" -ge 674679 ] || { echo "STOP: /var/cache/apt/archives needs 659 MB free for this plan, and has less. Free some room there (apt-get clean empties the cache of downloaded packages; remove what you do not need), then run this block again."; exit 1; }
[ "$(avail '/usr')" -ge 1488030 ] || { echo "STOP: /usr needs 1454 MB free for this plan, and has less. Free some room there (apt-get clean empties the cache of downloaded packages; remove what you do not need), then run this block again."; exit 1; }
[ "$(avail '/')" -ge 524288 ] || { echo "STOP: / needs 513 MB free for this plan, and has less. Free some room there (apt-get clean empties the cache of downloaded packages; remove what you do not need), then run this block again."; exit 1; }
isinst() { case "$(dpkg-query -W -f='${db:Status-Abbrev}' "$1" 2> /dev/null || true)" in ii*) return 0 ;; esac; return 1; }
[ "$(avail /boot)" -ge 307200 ] || { echo "STOP: /boot has less than 300 MiB free: the new kernel and its initrd are written there, and dpkg fails in the middle of block 6, after the point of no return, when there is no room. Free some room there (a kernel that you do not use any more, for example), then run this block again."; exit 1; }
if [ -d /sys/firmware/efi ]; then
  grep -q ' /boot/efi ' /proc/mounts || { echo "STOP: this machine starts with UEFI and the EFI system partition is not mounted on /boot/efi: GRUB would be written in the wrong place, or not at all. Mount it (see /etc/fstab), then run this block again."; exit 1; }
  [ "$(avail /boot/efi)" -ge 16384 ] || { echo "STOP: /boot/efi has less than 16 MiB free: GRUB's files are written there again. Free some room, then run this block again."; exit 1; }
elif isinst grub-pc; then
  devices="$(echo get grub-pc/install_devices | debconf-communicate 2> /dev/null | awk 'NR == 1 { $1 = ""; gsub(/[ ,]/, ""); print }' || true)"
  if [ -z "$devices" ]; then
    [ "$(echo get grub-pc/install_devices_empty | debconf-communicate 2> /dev/null | awk 'NR == 1 { print $2 }' || true)" = true ] || { echo "STOP: grub-pc has no disk to be installed on (grub-pc/install_devices is empty), and its update ends in error in block 6, where there is no terminal to ask it. Set it first: dpkg-reconfigure grub-pc   then run this block again."; exit 1; }
  fi
fi
# the sources of apt are the ones the plan was made from
srchash() {
  nl="$(printf '\nx')"; nl="${nl%x}"
  ( cd /etc/apt
  for f in sources.list sources.list.d/*; do
    [ -f "$f" ] || continue
    case "$f" in
      sources.list) ;;
      sources.list.d/*)
        name="${f#sources.list.d/}"
        case "$name" in *"$nl"*) continue ;; esac
        printf '%s\n' "$name" | grep -Eq '^[A-Za-z0-9_:-][A-Za-z0-9_:.-]*\.(list|sources)$' || continue ;;
    esac
    n="$(wc -c < "$f")"
    printf '%s\0%s\0' "$f" "$((n))"
    cat "$f"
    printf '\0'
  done ) | sha256sum | awk '{ print $1 }'
}
now="$(srchash)"
[ "$now" = '5a2a336dc446b8d1ba41147bc3a8f2bbe0e471ddc6463a2fcea5a1b808d83593' ] || { echo "STOP: the sources of apt are not the ones the plan was made from: something changed them. Ask for a new plan."; exit 1; }
if command -v dkms > /dev/null 2>&1 && [ -n "$(dkms status 2> /dev/null || true)" ]; then echo "WARNING: dkms has modules built from source on this machine (dkms status lists them). Block 6 builds them again for the new kernel, and a driver that does not build for it is a driver that is missing after the restart (a network card, a disk controller). This is NOT a stop: check by hand that each one supports the kernel of bookworm before you go on."; fi
mkdir -p -m 700 "$BK"; chmod 700 "$BK"
: > "$BK/done-verify"
echo "Block 0 done."
)
# <<< END BLOCK 0

# ==============================
# BLOCK 1 (of the blocks 0 to 8): stop the timers of apt and unattended-upgrades
# They would start an update in the middle of the hop. Their state is kept in a file the first time this block runs, and block 8 puts back the ones that were running and then removes the file.
# The file is written under a name of its own and put in place all at once (ln; a rename where ln cannot): two runs at the same time keep the state of the one that put it in place first, and none loses a line.
# The file is /var/backups/casaos-os-upgrade-timers.state, outside the folder of the plan on purpose: the plan has another id (and another folder) as soon as you change a removal, a hold or a source, and the second block 1 would
# find the timers stopped already. Run again, by this plan or by another, the block keeps that first state: the timers it stopped are not written down as stopped. To give up the hop, start them again:
# systemctl start $(awk '$2 == "active" { print $1 }' /var/backups/casaos-os-upgrade-timers.state)   then:   rm -f /var/backups/casaos-os-upgrade-timers.state
# They are enabled units, so a restart in the middle of the hop brings them back: blocks 3, 5 and 6 stop them again when they begin.
# ==============================
# >>> BLOCK 1 timers
(
set -eu
LC_ALL=C; export LC_ALL
PATH=/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin; export PATH
BK=/var/backups/casaos-os-upgrade-p1-3f419de2f78c0f350957a354740452ff
[ ! -e "$BK/done-after" ] || { echo "STOP: the hop is over (block 8 ended: done-after is in $BK): there is nothing more to run in this text."; exit 1; }
for fin in /var/backups/casaos-os-upgrade-*; do
  [ ! -e "$fin/done-after" ] || { echo "STOP: the hop is over for this machine: the plan whose folder is $fin took it to the end (block 8 ended: done-after is there), and there is nothing more to run in this text."; exit 1; }
done
[ -e "$BK/begun-upgrade" ] || [ -e "$BK/done-minimal" ] || grep -q '^VERSION_CODENAME=bullseye$' /etc/os-release || { echo "STOP: the hop is over for this machine: it is not Debian 11 (bullseye) any more, and this plan did not begin the upgrade of its packages (neither begun-upgrade nor done-minimal is in $BK): another plan, or the owner by hand, took it on, and nothing in this text applies to it. If another plan of this machine has not ended (ls /var/backups), go on with that one."; exit 1; }
[ -e "$BK/done-verify" ] || { echo "STOP: the block before this one (verify) did not end: run it first (ls $BK shows how far you got)."; exit 1; }
mkdir -p -m 700 "$BK"; chmod 700 "$BK"
TS=/var/backups/casaos-os-upgrade-timers.state
echo "Block 1: stopping the timers of apt."
if [ -e "$TS" ]; then
  echo "$TS is there from an earlier run of this block (by this plan or by another): the state of the timers that it holds is the one of before the hop, and it is kept."
else
  ( umask 077; : > "$TS.$$" )
  for unit in apt-daily.timer apt-daily-upgrade.timer unattended-upgrades.service; do
    printf '%s %s\n' "$unit" "$(systemctl is-active "$unit" 2>/dev/null || true)" >> "$TS.$$"
  done
  if ! ln "$TS.$$" "$TS" 2> /dev/null; then
    if [ -e "$TS" ]; then
      echo "$TS was put in place by another run of this block while this one was reading the timers: the state of that run is the one that is kept."
    else
      echo "ln could not put $TS in place (a file system with no hard links, or no room for one more entry): the state that this run wrote down is kept by a rename instead."
      mv -f "$TS.$$" "$TS" || { rm -f "$TS.$$"; echo "STOP: the state of the timers could not be put in $TS (is the disk full: df -h /var/backups): without it block 8 would start no timer. Free some room, then run this block again."; exit 1; }
    fi
  fi
  rm -f "$TS.$$"
fi
for unit in apt-daily.timer apt-daily-upgrade.timer unattended-upgrades.service; do
  if [ "$(systemctl is-active "$unit" 2>/dev/null || true)" = active ]; then systemctl stop "$unit"; fi
  [ "$(systemctl is-active "$unit" 2>/dev/null || true)" != active ] || { echo "STOP: $unit is still running: stop it (systemctl stop $unit), then run this block again."; exit 1; }
done
: > "$BK/done-timers"
echo "Block 1 done."
)
# <<< END BLOCK 1

# ==============================
# BLOCK 2 (of the blocks 0 to 8): write down the state of the machine
# A copy of what describes the machine now, in /var/backups/casaos-os-upgrade-<plan id> (private to root, mode 700; the copy of /etc in it is mode 600):
# the packages and their holds, /etc, the ports that listen, the settings of sshd, the iptables alternative, the units that fail now, the ReCasaOS units, the containers and their restart policy.
# It is not a backup of your data. Block 7 compares the settings of sshd, the iptables alternative and the kernel that runs with what is written down here; block 8 compares the ports that listen and the units that fail,
# and shows the ReCasaOS units and the containers beside the lists of before (it does not compare those two: you look).
# The lists of packages (selections.txt, packages.tsv) and the copy of /etc are for you to look at by hand: nothing in this text compares them.
# Run again after block 3 has begun, it stops: it would replace the state of the machine as it was with the state of now.
# ==============================
# >>> BLOCK 2 snapshot
(
set -eu
LC_ALL=C; export LC_ALL
PATH=/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin; export PATH
BK=/var/backups/casaos-os-upgrade-p1-3f419de2f78c0f350957a354740452ff
[ ! -e "$BK/done-after" ] || { echo "STOP: the hop is over (block 8 ended: done-after is in $BK): there is nothing more to run in this text."; exit 1; }
for fin in /var/backups/casaos-os-upgrade-*; do
  [ ! -e "$fin/done-after" ] || { echo "STOP: the hop is over for this machine: the plan whose folder is $fin took it to the end (block 8 ended: done-after is there), and there is nothing more to run in this text."; exit 1; }
done
